label: Yes
definition: They say the goal was achieved, or describe getting what they wanted, with no part of the goal left unmet.
include: Yes; I achieved my goal; it answered my questions; I think so; yes, even though it told me to see a doctor.
exclude: They name a part of their goal that was not met (B2). Hedged answers such as "mostly", "for the most part" or "in a sense" (B2, G10).
close_call: "Yes, but it told me to see a doctor" is B1 if they still say the goal was met, and the chat ALSO gets the tag "Told to see a doctor" (G11). "I think so" is B1: it is unsure wording, not a statement that only part of the goal was met. Doubts about AI in general ("it always validates me") do not change a yes.

label: Partly
definition: They say the goal was only partly met, use a hedge about how much was met ("mostly", "for the most part", "in a sense"), or say yes/sort of but name a part of the goal that was not met.
include: Partially; mostly achieved; for the most part; achieved in a sense; sort of, but I did not get answers; less fulfilling than I hoped.
exclude: A plain yes with only a general caveat about AI or doctors (B1). A clear no (B3). A conversation that is still going on with no judgement yet (B4).
close_call: Any hedge about HOW MUCH of the goal was met is B2, even if nothing is named as missing (G10).

label: No
definition: They say the goal was not achieved.
include: No; not really; not at all.
exclude: Answers that say "not as much as I hoped" but still say yes (B2).

label: Unclear
definition: The answer does not say whether the goal was met (blank, off-topic, only describes feelings without a judgement, or says the conversation is still going on).
include: Blank; answers about something else; it's a continuing conversation with progress still to make.
exclude: Answers that describe a clear result ("my headache was gone") are B1 even without the word yes.
close_call: Use only when no judgement can be read from the answer. An ongoing conversation is B4 (G12).
